pages.text: "Hot! Yum! Gulp!" Coco bit into a whole crescent loaf fresh from the oven, the big fiery place where bread bakes. Gulp, without chewing. Then another big bite! "I want to eat the most while it's warm!"
Coco's cheeks bulged. "Eat faster, eat more!" Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, chuckled by the door. Mom's eyebrows rose a little.
Then suddenly—hic! Hic! Coco had swallowed so fast that the hiccups wouldn't stop. Their shoulders jerked, and both front paws held their throat. "Mooom..."

Mom stroked Coco's back and offered a cup of water. "One sip at a time. Slowly." Coco's shoulders settled, and the hiccups stopped. "Your bites were too big. Shall we learn to eat slowly?" Coco nodded.
Mom whispered, "There's a tiny dough table inside your mouth. Your teeth need to knead ten times, just like kneading dough. Then the bread goes down softly." Grandpa added, "I chew ten times too."
"A bite as small as your front paw." Mom held a piece of bread beside Coco's paw. Then she sang, "Small bites, ten good chews!" Grandpa offered to count. "One, two..."
Coco broke off a paw-sized piece and chewed well. "One, two, three..." Grandpa counted while Coco chewed. "...Ten!" "Oh? The more I chew, the tastier it is!" Small bites, ten good chews!
After the bread, Coco's tummy felt comfortable. No hiccups either. Coco patted their tummy with both paws. "When I eat slowly, I don't get hiccups!"
Now Coco could do it alone. "One, a paw-sized bite! Two, ten good chews! Three, swallow when I've finished chewing!" Next morning, Coco broke the bread into paw-sized bites and counted, one, two.
Mom hugged Coco tight and patted their back. Small bites and good chewing make food tastier and easier on your throat. In Mom's arms, Coco called, "Small bites, ten good chews!"
